title: PLAYER MOVES — A temporary exhibition about how we play, 14 deliverables

config.text:
# PLAYER MOVES

## Identity and visit
- Exhibition name: PLAYER MOVES
- Entrance question: How do you play?
- Exhibition type: temporary digital culture exhibition
- Route order: Turn, Press, Move
- Typical visit: 20 minutes
- Planning occupancy: 18 visitors
- Activity duration: 60 seconds per station
- Automatic reset: 5 seconds after each activity
- Public interpretation language: English
- Content labels: Collection object; Archive content; New diagram
- Activity heading: Try the action
- Exhibit body limit: 45 words
- Exhibit label body size: 24 pt

## Room
- Coordinate origin: southwest internal corner
- Coordinates: x increases east; y increases north
- Internal dimensions: 12000 × 8000 mm
- Clear height: 3200 mm
- Entry: south wall, x = 0–1800 mm
- Exit: south wall, x = 10200–12000 mm
- Entry and exit clear height: 2400 mm
- South circulation strip: x = 0–12000 mm; y = 0–1800 mm
- South circulation strip clear width: 1800 mm
- Connecting route minimum clear width: 1500 mm
- Turning spaces: two circles, each 1500 mm diameter
- Archive display band: x = 1200–10800 mm; y = 5600–7400 mm
- Play zone: x = 2400–9600 mm; y = 2400–4800 mm
- Power points: north wall at (3000, 8000), (6000, 8000), (9000, 8000) mm
- Power distribution: surface cable covers along bench backs and room edges
- Seats: two movable seats, each with an adjacent 900 × 1200 mm clear space
- Room finishes: pale grey floor, off-white walls, exposed grey ceiling

## Equipment and interpretation
- Collection: E01–E03; three sets; one controller and one console per set; six collection objects total
- Archive benches: three; one set per bench
- Activity benches: three; one teaching controller and one screen per bench
- Teaching controllers: rotary knob, directional pad, motion handset
- Touch access: teaching controllers at all three activity benches
- Collection protection: one transparent lift-off cover per archive bench; three covers total
- Cover outer dimensions: 1100 × 500 × 350 mm
- Cover storage: one padded sleeve per cover; three sleeves total
- Screen count: three
- Screen logical layout: one instruction, one action diagram and one response area
- Screen content source: activity and interface records in 03-collection-records.md
- Open state: collection covers fitted; teaching controllers available; three screens active
- Closed state: collection covers fitted; teaching controllers secured below bench tops; three screens dark
- Bench top height: 800 mm
- Graphic centre height: 1400 mm
- Maximum freestanding height: 1800 mm
- Activity knee space: 900 mm wide × 600 mm deep × 700 mm high

## Six-bench kit
- Bench count: six
- Bench top dimensions: 1200 × 600 × 18 mm
- Main parts per bench: 12
- Legs per bench: four aluminium sections, each 782 × 40 × 40 mm
- Rails per bench: two aluminium sections, each 1200 × 40 × 40 mm; two aluminium sections, each 600 × 40 × 40 mm
- Top per bench: one birch plywood panel, 1200 × 600 × 18 mm
- Graphic supports per bench: two aluminium sections, each 1200 × 40 × 40 mm
- Graphic panel per bench: one interchangeable panel, 1200 × 600 × 6 mm
- Main parts total: 72
- Connections: 32 captive M6 socket bolts per bench; 192 total
- Assembly tool: 5 mm hex key
- Maximum detached main-part envelope: 1200 × 600 × 60 mm
- Cases: six; one dismantled bench per case
- Case external dimensions: 1250 × 650 × 650 mm
- Loose equipment transport: three cover sleeves and three padded equipment bags, one bag per exhibit set

This table lists every commissioned deliverable with its tier, file format and stage. What each deliverable must contain is stated in the commission letter.

| # | id | Deliverable | Tiers | Format and stage |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | label-copy | Label and activity copy table | 14 | Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: process. |
| 3 | route-plan | Dimensioned floor and visitor-route plan | 14 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 4 | elevation-section | Coordinated elevation and section | 14 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 5 | timeline-graphic | Three-example timeline graphic | 14 | Format: PNG, 1920 by 1080 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 6 | display-details | Controller and interface display details | 14 | Format: PNG, 2400 by 1600 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 7 | interaction-storyboard | Three-station interaction storyboard | 14 | Format: PNG, 2400 by 1600 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 8 | entrance-view | Visitor view from the entrance | 14 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 9 | exit-view | Visitor view from Move towards the exit | 14 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 10 | open-state | Open exhibition state | 14 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 11 | closed-state | Closed exhibition state | 14 | Format: PNG, 1800 by 1200 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 12 | assembly-packing | Assembly, dismantling and packing sheet | 14 | Format: PNG, 2400 by 1600 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 13 | route-video | Ten-second visitor-route video | 14 | Format: video; 5 to 15 seconds. Stage: final. |
| 14 | presentation | Exhibition presentation and catalogue | 14 | Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final. |

# PLAYER MOVES collection and interpretation records

## Collection register

Dimensions are width × depth × height in mm. Years identify the collection examples. Route order is Turn, Press, Move.

| ID | Exhibit name | Year | Zone | Controller dimensions | Console dimensions | Bench assignments |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E01 | Rotary paddle and console | 1978 | Turn | 70 × 110 × 55 | 340 × 220 × 80 | Archive 1; Activity 1 |
| E02 | Directional pad and console | 1986 | Press | 125 × 55 × 20 | 260 × 200 × 75 | Archive 2; Activity 2 |
| E03 | Motion handset and console | 2007 | Move | 40 × 150 × 35 | 160 × 210 × 45 | Archive 3; Activity 3 |

## Object appearance

| ID | Controller | Console |
|---|---|---|
| E01 | Black rectangular handheld body; one large black rotary knob; one orange side button; fixed cable | Low black rectangular enclosure; brown front trim; four small silver switches across the top front edge |
| E02 | Pale grey rectangular pad; black cross-shaped directional control on the left; two red round buttons on the right; fixed cable | Pale grey rectangular enclosure; dark grey front band; one horizontal front cartridge opening |
| E03 | White elongated handset; black cross-shaped directional control; one large circular face button; wrist strap | White flat rectangular enclosure; narrow black front disc opening; one small circular power button |

## Exhibit labels

Title structure: ID / exhibit name / year. Body limit: 45 words per exhibit.

| ID | Title | Exact body |
|---|---|---|
| E01 | E01 / Rotary paddle and console / 1978 | Turning the knob changes the paddle position continuously. Small hand movements become small movements on screen. Follow the moving target and notice how your wrist controls distance. |
| E02 | E02 / Directional pad and console / 1986 | Four directions turn movement into separate choices. Your thumb selects a direction while another finger operates a button. Compare these distinct presses with the continuous turning action in Turn. |
| E03 | E03 / Motion handset and console / 2007 | The handset makes movement of the controller part of the input. Tilt the teaching handset and watch the marker travel. Compare moving your hand through space with pressing a direction in Press. |

## Archive interface records

| Record | Exhibit | Interface description | Exact archive excerpt | Content label |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A01 | E01 | Dark field; bright vertical paddle beside the left edge; one bright square target | Turning the control moves the paddle up or down. | Archive content |
| A02 | E02 | Side-view field; one player marker; horizontal ground line; directional movement and a separate action | The directional control moves the player. The action button triggers a separate move. | Archive content |
| A03 | E03 | Pointer field; one cursor; three target circles; controller movement changes the cursor position | Move the controller to move the pointer across the screen. | Archive content |

## Teaching activities

| Exhibit | Heading | Exact instruction | Action | Visible response | Duration | Reset |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E01 | Try the action | Turn the knob to follow the target. | Rotary teaching knob turns left or right | A vertical bar moves continuously towards a moving square target | 60 seconds | 5 seconds; bar returns to centre |
| E02 | Try the action | Press a direction, then press the round button. | Directional teaching pad selects one of four directions; round button confirms | A marker moves one grid cell per press; confirmation fills the selected cell | 60 seconds | 5 seconds; grid clears and marker returns to centre |
| E03 | Try the action | Tilt the handset to guide the marker. | Strapped teaching handset tilts left or right through a limited seated or standing movement | A marker moves horizontally towards one of three targets | 60 seconds | 5 seconds; marker returns to centre |

## Content labels
- Physical controller-and-console pairs: Collection object
- Archive excerpts A01–A03: Archive content
- Newly drawn interface explanations: New diagram
- Teaching activity instructions: Try the action

steps.userMessage:
PLAYER MOVES | A temporary exhibition about how we play

We are commissioning a temporary exhibition for visitors who know contemporary games but may never have handled an early controller. The exhibition follows three collection examples in this order: Turn, Press, Move. These are dated examples of different interactions: E01, Rotary paddle and console, 1978; E02, Directional pad and console, 1986; and E03, Motion handset and console, 2007. Each example pairs two collection objects with one hands-on teaching controller and one screen. A typical visit lasts 20 minutes, including a 60-second activity at each station. Print "PLAYER MOVES" and "How do you play?" at the entrance. Collection objects, archive excerpts and newly drawn explanations carry the labels "Collection object", "Archive content" and "New diagram" respectively; activity instructions begin with "Try the action".

The room is 12000 mm east–west by 8000 mm north–south, with a clear height of 3200 mm. Entry and exit occupy opposite ends of the south wall, each 1800 mm wide. The south circulation strip stays 1800 mm clear; connecting routes are at least 1500 mm clear. Three archive benches occupy the north display band and three activity benches occupy the central play zone shown on the attached plan. Bench tops are 800 mm above the floor, graphic centres are 1400 mm above the floor and freestanding elements reach at most 1800 mm. Our six-bench kit uses aluminium rails and legs, birch plywood tops and interchangeable graphic panels, joined with M6 bolts using a 5 mm hex key. It has 72 main parts and 192 bolts, packs into six cases and has a largest detached part of 1200 × 600 × 60 mm. Build the exhibit register and label copy first, then develop the route, interpretation and installation from those two documents.

Audience: the exhibition producer, interpretation team and installation crew, for approving the visitor experience and planning the temporary build.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the room, visitor, interaction and kit facts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable with its proportion, format and stage. 03-collection-records.md contains the exhibit names, dates, dimensions, label bodies, archive excerpts and activity records. room-constraints.png fixes the room boundary, doors, circulation strip, power points and equipment zones. collection-equipment.png records the recognisable forms of the three controller-and-console sets. empty-room.png provides the room's material and daylight atmosphere. waiting-visitors.png provides the scale and social spacing of a small group waiting to take turns.

Deliverables:
1. A two-page exhibit register and route schedule covering E01–E03, their names, dates, dimensions, Turn–Press–Move sequence, bench assignments and installation heights
2. A two-page label copy table containing three exhibit titles and bodies, three archive excerpts, three activity instructions and the four content labels, with a 45-word limit for each exhibit body
3. One dimensioned floor and visitor-route plan with E01–E03 names and dates, zone names, six benches, three screens, power routes, two seats and clear passage widths
4. One coordinated elevation and section sheet with bench tops, graphic centres, screen positions, knee spaces and maximum installation height
5. One continuous timeline graphic connecting the three dated examples to turning, pressing and moving, with the entrance title and question
6. One display-detail sheet covering all three controller-and-console pairs, their complete exhibit labels, archive excerpts and newly drawn interface explanations
7. One interaction storyboard sheet covering the instruction, action, response and reset of all three 60-second activities
8. Two visitor-eye spatial views, one from the entrance towards Turn and one from Move towards the exit
9. Two operational-state drawings of the same installation, one open and one closed, showing collection covers, teaching controllers and screen states
10. One assembly and packing sheet showing the six-bench kit, material assignments, bolted joints, component counts, dismantling sequence and six packed cases
11. One 10-second visitor-route video moving through Turn, Press and Move and ending with the exhibition name
12. One presentation document of at least 10 pages, reusing the register, copy table, drawings, graphics, activity sequence and spatial views, with a three-exhibit catalogue and a fact-to-deliverable index

Acceptance:
- The exhibit register establishes E01–E03, Turn–Press–Move order, 800 mm bench tops and 1400 mm graphic centres; the floor plan repeats the IDs and zone order, the elevation repeats both heights, and the presentation repeats all four facts.
- The label copy table, display-detail sheet and presentation catalogue reproduce all three ID–name–year combinations and exhibit bodies from 03-collection-records.md; each body stays within 45 words. The display-detail sheet places Collection object beside each physical pair, Archive content beside each supplied excerpt and New diagram beside each new interface explanation.
- The floor plan, elevation, two visitor-eye views and two state drawings describe the same six-bench installation within the 12000 × 8000 × 3200 mm room. The drawings dimension the 1800 mm south strip, connecting routes of at least 1500 mm, two 1500 mm turning spaces, two seats, activity knee spaces of 900 × 600 × 700 mm and the 1800 mm height limit.
- The interaction storyboard begins each activity with Try the action and shows the recorded action, visible response, 60-second duration and 5-second reset for E01–E03. The open-state drawing shows three active screens and three available teaching controllers; the closed-state drawing shows three dark screens and three secured teaching controllers, with collection covers fitted in both states.
- The assembly and packing sheet accounts for six benches, 72 main parts, 192 M6 bolts, a 5 mm hex key and six 1250 × 650 × 650 mm cases; its exploded views identify aluminium, birch plywood and graphic panels, and its packing views retain the 1200 × 600 × 60 mm maximum detached-part envelope.
- The timeline graphic, entrance visitor-eye view and presentation print PLAYER MOVES and How do you play? The 10-second video follows Turn, Press, Move and ends with PLAYER MOVES. The presentation contains at least 10 pages and identifies the deliverable carrying each room, collection, interaction and kit fact.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
